about.title: About Me
bio: Full-stack developer with a unique foundation in mathematics, cryptography, and logic — skills that turn complex problems into clean, scalable code. Self-taught and relentlessly curious, I bridge creative front-end design and robust back-end architecture.

Frontend: React, Next.js (App Router), TypeScript and TailwindCSS. Backend: Node.js, Express and NestJS — modular, type-safe REST APIs with JWT authentication, role-based permissions and Swagger docs. Data: PostgreSQL with Prisma ORM, MongoDB, and Redis for caching and queues. DevOps: Dockerized services, CI/CD with GitHub Actions, Linux servers behind Nginx, and deployments on Vercel. WordPress: 50+ websites delivered for government institutions.

I don't just build components — I architect complete solutions, from the database schema to the deployed application. Fluent in English, French, and Arabic, I communicate clearly with European and international clients. Independent, persistent, and passionate about turning ideas into production-ready web applications. Let's build something great together.

caseStudyLabels.ctaText: Need a platform like this for your organization?

projectItems.title: Architectural Association Management Platform
projectItems.description: A full-featured management platform for a national architectural association handling 10,000+ members. Automates member validation, financial tracking, penalty calculations, and dynamic PDF document generation with customizable templates and QR codes for official receipts, financial statements, and diplomas.

caseStudy.tagline: A management platform for a national architectural association: member validation, dues and penalties, permissions, statistics and official PDF documents, all in one place.
caseStudy.context: A national association of architects has to keep track of more than 10,000 members: validating new registrations, collecting yearly dues, applying late-payment penalties and issuing official documents such as receipts, financial statements and diplomas. Handling all of that across spreadsheets and paperwork is slow and error-prone.
caseStudy.role: I designed and built the platform end to end: the PostgreSQL schema with Prisma, the NestJS REST API with authentication and permissions, the React admin dashboard, and the PDF document-generation pipeline.

features.title: Member validation
features.text: Registration requests go through a validation workflow before a member becomes active.

features.title: Dues tracking
features.text: Each member's yearly contributions (cotisations) and payment history in one view.

features.title: Automatic penalties
features.text: Late-payment penalties are calculated automatically from the association's rules.

features.title: Permissions
features.text: Role-based access control decides who can view, validate or edit each part of the platform.

features.title: Official PDF documents
features.text: Receipts, financial statements and diplomas generated from customizable templates, each with a QR code.

features.title: Statistics dashboard
features.text: Live figures on members, payments and outstanding balances for the association's board.

challenges.title: Pixel-perfect official documents
challenges.text: Receipts and diplomas must look identical every time. Documents are built from customizable HTML templates and rendered to PDF with headless Chrome (Puppeteer), with a QR code embedded so each document can be checked.

challenges.title: Consistent financial data
challenges.text: Dues and penalties are calculated on the server, never in the browser, so every receipt and statement is based on the same source of truth in PostgreSQL.

challenges.title: Fine-grained access
challenges.text: Different staff roles need different powers. Permissions are enforced in the API itself, not just hidden in the UI, so a request without the right role is rejected.

projectItems.title: MBS Solutions — Corporate Website
projectItems.description: The bilingual (French/English) corporate website of MBS Solutions, an Algerian IT engineering company. Built with Next.js, it presents the company's services, platforms, history and clients, with smooth animations and a contact form that emails the team directly.

caseStudy.tagline: A fast, bilingual Next.js website that presents an IT engineering company to businesses and public administrations, and turns visitors into leads.
caseStudy.context: MBS Solutions builds software platforms (GestOrg, Khabir, E-GED) and IT services for organizations, professional bodies and administrations in Algeria and abroad. The company needed a modern website that explains what it does, shows the clients that trust it, and makes it easy to request a quote, in both French and English.
caseStudy.role: I designed and developed the website: page structure and UI, the translation system, the animations, and the contact form backend.

features.title: Bilingual content
features.text: All text lives in French and English dictionaries, switched instantly from the navbar without reloading the page.

features.title: Services catalogue
features.text: Seven service offerings, each opening a detailed view of what is included.

features.title: Platforms & projects
features.text: Showcases the company's platforms (GestOrg, Khabir, E-GED) with descriptions and features.

features.title: Company timeline
features.text: An animated history of the company, from its founding in 2018 to its international offices.

features.title: Client logos
features.text: A scrolling band of organizations that work with MBS, for instant credibility.

features.title: Contact form & map
features.text: A validated form with a completion counter that emails the team, plus an embedded Google Map.

architecture.name: Email
parts: Message delivered to the team inbox

challenges.title: A contact form without exposing secrets
challenges.text: The form posts to a Next.js API route that validates the fields and sends the email with Nodemailer on the server. SMTP credentials stay in environment variables and never reach the browser.

challenges.title: Two languages, one codebase
challenges.text: Instead of duplicating pages, every component reads its text from a shared translation context backed by French and English JSON files, so adding content means editing data, not code.

challenges.title: Motion that stays fast
challenges.text: Sections animate into view with Framer Motion only once, when they appear on screen, keeping the site lively without hurting performance.

projectItems.title: 50+ Government Websites (WordPress)
projectItems.description: More than 50 WordPress websites built for government institutions: official, responsive sites that non-technical staff can update themselves, delivered quickly and consistently.

caseStudy.tagline: Over 50 official websites for public institutions, built on WordPress so every organization gets a professional site its own staff can keep up to date.
caseStudy.context: Government institutions need an official web presence to publish news, announcements, documents and contact information. Each one needs a credible, consistent site that its own team can update without calling a developer.
caseStudy.role: I built and delivered the websites: setting up WordPress, designing and configuring the themes, structuring the content, and handing over sites that staff can manage on their own.

features.title: Official, consistent design
features.text: A professional look adapted to each institution's identity, with a consistent structure across sites.

features.title: Easy content updates
features.text: Staff publish news, announcements and pages from the WordPress dashboard, without technical knowledge.

features.title: Responsive on every device
features.text: Every site works on phones, tablets and desktops.

features.title: Repeatable delivery
features.text: A proven setup process makes it possible to deliver many sites quickly while keeping quality consistent.

challenges.title: Delivering at scale
challenges.text: Building more than 50 sites means turning the setup into a repeatable process, so each new institution gets a reliable, polished site quickly.

challenges.title: Built for non-technical editors
challenges.text: The sites are structured so the people who update them every day can do it confidently from the WordPress dashboard.
